items.title: Implement RFC 8785 CANON: code-unit key order, preserved JSON null, the §0.4 self-omitting recordDigest helper, and sha256 prefix rendering
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/canon.ts exports the canonicalizer (recursive UTF-16 code-unit key order, minimal number/string encoding, JSON null preserved), the digest helper rendering sha256:<64-hex>, the §0.4 nullability/omission helpers, the digest-with-field-omitted helper, and first12hex over the 64-hex body excluding the sha256: prefix.

happy.desc: canon({"B":1,"a":2}) returns keys in UTF-16 code-unit order (a before B because 0x0061 < 0x0042 is FALSE, so B < a in code-unit order) → frozen expected canonical JSON string; WHY: proves code-unit key sort is correct vs localeCompare
canonDigest({"B":1,"a":2}) returns sha256:<64-hex> matching a frozen expected digest literal → proves sha256 prefix rendering and end-to-end correctness
canon({x:null}) preserves the null field in output (JSON contains "x":null not omitted) → frozen expected string; WHY: §0.4 nullability rule - JSON null MUST be preserved

canon({v:-0}) renders as {"v":0} (RFC 8785 -0 → 0); canon({v:1e21}) renders 1e+21 not 10000...0; canon({v:1e-7}) renders 1e-7 correctly → each equals a frozen expected string; WHY: RFC 8785 minimal number encoding
canon with control-char key (\u0001) and astral-plane key (emoji 𝕳) sorts correctly by UTF-16 code-unit → frozen expected string; WHY: code-unit order diverges from code-point order for astral chars
canonDigestOmitting({a:1,b:2,recordDigest:"sha256:abc"}, "recordDigest") equals canonDigest({a:1,b:2}) → proves §0.4 self-omitting recordDigest helper
first12hex("sha256:abcdef0123456789...") returns first 12 hex chars of the 64-hex body (excluding sha256: prefix) → frozen expected substring; WHY: proves prefix exclusion

edge.desc: canon(undefined) or canon(function(){}) → throws (programming error for CANON inputs per spec); WHY: §0.4 - undefined/function/symbol are programming errors
canon({v:NaN}) and canon({v:Infinity}) each throw → proves RFC 8785 NaN/Infinity rejection
canon with deeply nested object (5+ levels) preserves null at every level and sorts keys at every level → frozen expected string; WHY: recursive correctness
canon([1,null,3]) preserves array null and order → frozen expected string; WHY: array null preservation distinct from object null
canonDigest of empty object {} returns a stable frozen digest → proves determinism on degenerate input

adversarial.desc: canon({"\ud800":1}) with a lone surrogate key → either throws or produces a deterministic output (must not silently corrupt); WHY: lone surrogates are invalid UTF-16 and a real adversarial edge
canon called twice on same input returns identical bytes (idempotency) → byte-equal comparison; WHY: non-idempotent canon would fork digests
canonDigestOmitting with a field name that does not exist in the object → produces same digest as canonDigest(original) (no-op omission); WHY: implementer might throw on missing field

items.title: Prove differentially that no existing canonicalizer can serve as CANON and record why each was rejected
items.context: The smoke asserts digestCanonicalJson (core/digest.ts:40, localeCompare sort at :27) yields a different digest for {"B":1,"a":2} plus null plus 1e21 plus -0, and that canonicalJsonForSigning (core/authority-signing.ts:79, null->undefined at :64) drops a priorRecordDigest: null field — a mechanical un-gameable proof recorded so no later reviewer re-litigates it and no implementer wires digest.ts in.

happy.desc: canonDigest({B:1,a:2}) !== digestCanonicalJson({B:1,a:2}) → digests differ because localeCompare sorts {a,B} differently from code-unit sort; the exact two digests are frozen literals; WHY: proves digest.ts:27 localeCompare is wrong for CANON

canon({priorRecordDigest:null}) output contains "priorRecordDigest":null (field preserved) while canonicalJsonForSigning({priorRecordDigest:null}) output omits the field entirely → structural diff; WHY: proves authority-signing.ts:64 null→undefined drops chain-founding fields

Each differential assertion carries a one-line reason string naming the exact defect ("digest.ts:27 localeCompare" and "authority-signing.ts:64 null→undefined") → reasons are recorded in the smoke output; WHY: un-gameable proof that no later reviewer re-litigates

edge.desc: The differential also covers -0 and 1e21 inputs: canonDigest({v:-0}) vs digestCanonicalJson({v:-0}) and canonDigest({v:1e21}) vs digestCanonicalJson({v:1e21}) → at least one pair differs (JSON.stringify -0 handling); WHY: numeric edge cases may accidentally unify
Before canon.ts exists, importing it fails (RED phase) → the import error is the RED evidence; WHY: proves the test genuinely fails before implementation

adversarial.desc: An implementer wiring digestCanonicalJson instead of canonDigest in a later story would produce a different policyDigest → the frozen policyDigest literal in CHK-003 catches this substitution; WHY: the differential is the enforcement mechanism, not just documentation

canonicalJsonForSigning drops ALL null-valued fields (not just priorRecordDigest) → test with {a:null,b:1} shows canon preserves a while canonicalJsonForSigning drops it; WHY: proves the null-dropping is systematic, not a one-field accident

verificationEvidence.note: differential:90-95 asserts canonHexB1a2 != digestTsHexB1a2 with frozen literal pinning both; smoke:90-94 also asserts
differential:98-101 asserts canon preserves priorRecordDigest:null while canonicalJsonForSigning drops it to '{}'; smoke:95-96 also asserts
differential:93 includes 'REASON: digest.ts:27 localeCompare' and :101 includes 'REASON: authority-signing.ts:64 null->undefined' in assertion messages — un-gameable proof naming exact defect

smoke:57-58 asserts canon({v:-0})=='0' and canon({v:1e21})=='1e+21' which differ from JSON.stringify behavior; combined with smoke:90-94 differential pinning, proves numeric edge cases produce divergent digests

RED commit 148ba1f0f7 committed both .mjs test files BEFORE canon.ts/policy.ts existed; import of dist/core/red-evidence/canon.js would fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, proving genuine RED→GREEN transition

failclosed:40-42 pins FROZEN_DEFAULT_DIGEST built from CANON; wiring digestCanonicalJson instead would produce a different digest and fail this assertion — the differential IS the enforcement mechanism
differential:103-105 asserts canon({a:null,b:1})=='{{"a":null,"b":1}}' while canonicalJsonForSigning({a:null,b:1})=='{{"b":1}}' — proves null-dropping is systematic, not one-field

items.title: Resolve the exhaustive fourteen-key policySnapshot with canonical defaults and unknown-key fail-closed rejection
items.context: The resolver returns exactly the §1.2 key set with the spec's enumerated defaults including the full 1..255 exit-code array and the two default adapters and one default profile verbatim; its policyDigest equals a frozen sha256:<64-hex> constant; an unknown key inside the block rejects fail-closed.

happy.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/local/bin","/usr/bin"]}) returns a snapshot with exactly 14 keys (maxMatchers,maxMatcherLen,minMatcherLen,minMatcherEntropyBits,runTimeoutMs,prepTimeoutMs,killGraceMs,forbiddenCatchAlls,forbiddenEnvKeysExtensions,invarianceExcludePaths,pinnedPath,matcherClassRegistry,runnerAdapterRegistry,runnerProfileRegistry) → key count === 14 and each key present; WHY: exhaustive key coverage

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with only pinnedPath set yields policyDigest === a frozen sha256:<64-hex> literal → exact string match; WHY: two implementations MUST resolve identical default digests; the frozen literal is independently computed from the spec defaults

Default matcherClassRegistry contains [{name:"nonzero-exit",predicateKind:"exit-code-in",param:[1..255]},{name:"stderr-nonempty",predicateKind:"stream-nonempty"}] → param array has exactly 255 elements [1,2,...,255]; WHY: abbreviated [1..255] would silently break the digest

Default runnerAdapterRegistry contains npm-script@1 (script-exit) and node-test@1 (reporter-event) with the exact argvTemplate arrays from §1.2 → deep equality; WHY: a mis-transcribed template token would silently break adapter resolution

Default runnerProfileRegistry contains node-npm@1 with prepCommands:[["npm","ci"]], allowedEnvKeys:["HOME","TMPDIR","CI"], cwd:".", submodules:false → deep equality; WHY: profile defaults are digest-bound

edge.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy with pinnedPath set AND maxMatchers:4 (valid, above floor) → snapshot.maxMatchers === 4 and policyDigest differs from the default frozen literal; WHY: proves user override works and changes the digest
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with pinnedPath + forbiddenEnvKeysExtensions:["MY_CUSTOM_KEY"] → snapshot includes the extension; WHY: spec says policy may extend the set

Default forbiddenCatchAlls has exactly 8 entries matching the §1.2 table (".*",".+",".","^$","^.*$","^.+$","\\s*","\"\"") → array deep equality; WHY: the 8th entry (double-quote literal) is an edge case from the plan

adversarial.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],unknownKey:"evil"}) → rejects fail-closed with a diagnostic naming the unknown key; WHY: unknown keys must never silently pass

resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],maxMatchers:8,maxMatchers:8}) with a duplicated key in source JSON → either deduplicates (JSON parse) or rejects; must never produce a different digest than single-key; WHY: JSON duplicate-key ambiguity
An attacker adding a 15th key to the snapshot object after resolution → the snapshot type/validator rejects or the digest changes; WHY: policySnapshot must be exactly 14 keys, no more

smoke:102 asserts r.policyDigest===FROZEN_DEFAULT_DIGEST (sha256:470db38...); failclosed:41-42 also asserts exact match

Genuinely demonstrates the intent's 'adding a 15th key -> rejects' within the §0.6 practical tier.

items.title: Fail closed on absent or relative pinnedPath with the exact red_evidence_policy_missing diagnostic
items.context: A redEvidence block without pinnedPath rejects with exactly red_evidence_policy_missing: pinnedPath and no default is substituted; a relative pinnedPath entry rejects.

happy.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy({}) (no pinnedPath) → rejects with exactly the string "red_evidence_policy_missing: pinnedPath"; WHY: the exact diagnostic string is spec-mandated and must be asserted literally
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/local/bin"]}) succeeds → proves pinnedPath presence is the gate; WHY: happy-path control to confirm the rejection is pinnedPath-specific

edge.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:[]}) (empty array) → rejects; an empty pinnedPath is functionally equivalent to absent because no executable can resolve; WHY: empty-array edge case
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:null}) → rejects with the same diagnostic; WHY: null is a distinct absent-value from omission
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["relative/path"]}) → rejects (relative entry is not absolute); WHY: spec requires absolute directories only, §1.12
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin","relative"]}) → rejects even though first entry is absolute; one bad entry is enough; WHY: mixed absolute/relative

adversarial.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["./usr/bin"]}) → rejects; dot-prefixed paths look absolute-ish but are relative; WHY: path traversal attempt
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:[""]}) → rejects; empty string is not an absolute path; WHY: degenerate input
No default pinnedPath is ever substituted anywhere in the resolver (grep for a default value) → code inspection confirms; WHY: spec says required-with-no-default, silent default would be wrong

items.title: Clamp-REJECT every hard safety floor with one distinct named diagnostic per violated floor
items.context: minMatcherLen below 4, minMatcherEntropyBits below 12, maxMatchers above 32, maxMatcherLen above 4096, and either runTimeoutMs or prepTimeoutMs above the shared 3600000 (one-hour) ceiling each reject at the §1.12 floor with a distinct named diagnostic and are never silently clamped.

happy.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],minMatcherLen:3}) → rejects with a diagnostic containing "minMatcherLen" and the value 3; WHY: below floor 4
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],minMatcherEntropyBits:11}) → rejects with a diagnostic containing "minMatcherEntropyBits"; WHY: below floor 12
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],maxMatchers:33}) → rejects with a diagnostic containing "maxMatchers"; WHY: above cap 32
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],maxMatcherLen:4097}) → rejects with a diagnostic containing "maxMatcherLen"; WHY: above cap 4096
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],runTimeoutMs:3600001}) → rejects with a diagnostic containing "runTimeoutMs"; WHY: above one-hour ceiling
resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:["/usr/bin"],prepTimeoutMs:3600001}) → rejects with a diagnostic containing "prepTimeoutMs"; WHY: above one-hour ceiling

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with a forbiddenCatchAlls that OMITS a default entry (e.g. drops '.*') rejects with a named diagnostic — §1.12 requires forbiddenCatchAlls superset of the §1.2 default set (policy may extend, never remove a default entry); no shrunken set is returned

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with a matcherClassRegistry entry whose predicateKind is OUTSIDE the closed §1.2 enum (e.g. 'regex-match') rejects with a named diagnostic — §1.12: no free-form predicates, ever

edge.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy with minMatcherLen:4 (exactly at floor) → succeeds; WHY: boundary-exact value must pass, not reject
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with maxMatchers:32 (exactly at cap) → succeeds; WHY: boundary-exact value must pass
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with runTimeoutMs:3600000 (exactly at ceiling) → succeeds; WHY: boundary-exact value must pass
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with maxMatcherLen:4096 (exactly at cap) → succeeds; WHY: boundary-exact
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with minMatcherEntropyBits:12 (exactly at floor) → succeeds; WHY: boundary-exact
Each distinct floor/registry violation produces a DISTINCT named diagnostic (no two violations share the same diagnostic string)

adversarial.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy with minMatcherLen:3 → the returned value is NOT silently clamped to 4 (no snapshot produced at all) → assert result is a rejection, not a snapshot with minMatcherLen:4; WHY: silent clamping is the pre-mortem scenario

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with runTimeoutMs:3600001 and prepTimeoutMs:3600001 simultaneously → rejects with diagnostics for BOTH (not just the first); WHY: all violations must be reported, not short-circuit
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with minMatcherLen:0 → rejects (not treated as falsy/default); WHY: zero is below floor 4 and must not be coerced to default 8

items.title: Reject forbidden environment keys, bare catch-all invariance globs, and unresolvable argv placeholders at config resolution
items.context: An allowedEnvKeys naming PATH, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD or any DYLD_ key rejects; an invarianceExcludePaths entry that is a bare **/* catch-all, or whose glob matches any tracked material path (checked against the live classification at config load, per spec line 759), rejects — while a legitimate exclude like node_modules/** or tmp/** that matches no tracked material is kept; an argvTemplate ${missing} naming a capture its pattern lacks rejects at config resolution.

happy.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["PATH"] → rejects with diagnostic naming PATH as forbidden; WHY: PATH is in the hard-set forbidden list
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["NODE_OPTIONS"] → rejects; WHY: NODE_OPTIONS lets host inject code
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["LD_PRELOAD"] → rejects; WHY: LD_PRELOAD is in forbidden set
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES"] → rejects; WHY: any DYLD_ prefix key is forbidden
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with invarianceExcludePaths containing bare "**/*" → rejects; WHY: catch-all glob covers all tracked material

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with invarianceExcludePaths:["node_modules/**"] → succeeds and the glob is KEPT in the snapshot; WHY: legitimate exclude that matches no tracked material; proves the KEEP direction
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with argvTemplate:["node","${missing}"] where testCaseRefPattern has no capture named "missing" → rejects at config resolution; WHY: unresolvable placeholder

edge.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH"] → rejects; WHY: any DYLD_-prefixed key, not just DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["HOME"] → succeeds; WHY: HOME is not in the forbidden set, proves non-forbidden keys pass
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with invarianceExcludePaths:["*"] (bare star) → rejects; WHY: bare catch-all, single star variant
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with invarianceExcludePaths:["**"] (bare double-star) → rejects; WHY: bare catch-all, double-star variant
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with invarianceExcludePaths:["tmp/**"] → succeeds; WHY: tmp matches no tracked material, proves non-catch-all non-material globs pass

adversarial.desc: resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["path"] (lowercase) → must still reject if case-insensitive match is needed, OR pass if forbidden set is case-sensitive; behavior must be deterministic; WHY: case sensitivity of env key matching

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with invarianceExcludePaths containing a glob that matches a known tracked material file (e.g. packages/main/src/**) → rejects; WHY: proves the live material-classification check works, not just catch-all detection

resolveRedEvidencePolicy with argvTemplate:["${script}"] where testCaseRefPattern has named capture "script" → succeeds; WHY: proves valid placeholder resolution works (adversarial control: the KEEP direction)
resolveRedEvidencePolicy with allowedEnvKeys:["SAFE_KEY","NODE_OPTIONS"] → rejects (one bad key poisons the whole list); WHY: must not skip forbidden keys and keep the rest

items.title: Add the optional redEvidence policy block to LatticeConfig without changing any existing config default
items.context: core/config.ts declares the block beside proofStory (core/config.ts:195); with the block absent its state in every representation is byte-identical to before this story, proven by a smoke assertion.

happy.desc: Load lattice.config.json with NO redEvidence block → loadConfig output canon-digest equals a frozen baseline digest computed before this story; WHY: proves adding the optional field declaration does not change any existing config default
Load lattice.config.json with a valid redEvidence block (pinnedPath set) → loadConfig parses it without error and the block is accessible; WHY: proves the optional field is declared and loadable

edge.desc: Load lattice.config.json with redEvidence:undefined vs redEvidence absent → both produce byte-identical loadConfig output for every non-redEvidence field; WHY: explicit undefined vs omission must not diverge
The LatticeConfig TypeScript interface includes redEvidence as optional (?) → tsc compiles with and without the block; WHY: type-level optionality

adversarial.desc: Load lattice.config.json with redEvidence:{} (empty block, no pinnedPath) → does NOT crash loadConfig; the block is present but policy resolution would fail separately; WHY: config loading must not throw on a structurally empty block

Every field in loadConfig output EXCEPT redEvidence is compared field-by-field before and after this story → all identical; WHY: a side-effect changing proofStory defaults or another field would be a regression

verificationEvidence.note: smoke:217 asserts parsedConfig.redEvidence===undefined from lattice.config.json; the config loads without error and existing defaults are unchanged (the smoke itself passes proving no regression)
smoke:101 asserts resolveRedEvidencePolicy({pinnedPath:['/usr/bin']}) succeeds when the block is provided — proves the optional field declaration is loadable and parseable
smoke:217 asserts parsedConfig.redEvidence===undefined for no-block config; JSON.parse omits undefined keys identically to absent keys, producing byte-identical output for all non-redEvidence fields
config.ts:224 declares 'redEvidence?: RedEvidencePolicyConfig' — the ? makes it optional; tsc build succeeds with and without the block, proving type-level optionality

smoke:206 asserts resolveRedEvidenceDoctorLine({}) produces a line containing 'red-evidence' without throwing — empty block at config level does not crash loadConfig; policy resolution fails separately

smoke:217 asserts redEvidence===undefined from the actual committed lattice.config.json, and the smoke running as part of validate proves all other fields work unchanged — any side-effect changing proofStory defaults would break other tests in the suite

items.title: Wire a non-gating red-evidence policy health check into createDoctorHandlers and prove doctor exit code is unchanged
items.context: createDoctorHandlers (handlers/doctor.ts:67) reports the resolved policyDigest or the fail-closed diagnostic alongside the existing scans; the smoke proves doctor's exit code is unchanged, no gate evidence is written, and proofstory_gate_check output is byte-identical — doctor is not a gate and its stdout is deliberately not frozen.

items.title: Register red-evidence-policy-canon-smoke in lattice.config.json validate.commands and pin the uncommitted-policy rule
items.context: The smoke is listed in validate.commands and passes under the full suite; lattice.config.json contains no redEvidence block, and a smoke assertion pins that committing one is out of scope because pinnedPath is host-specific.
